1750.translation: I no sabi drive, so I dey enter bus.

1751.translation: -(으)ㄹ 줄 알다/모르다 mean to know or no know how to do something. -(으)면 안 되다 na prohibition, and -(으)면 되다 mean na enough to do am. -(으)ㄹ까요 with -아/어도 fit ask whether dem allow something. 못 or -지 못하다 dey show inability.

1752.translation: You must no talk loud for library.

1753.translation: Na only this button you need press.

1754.translation: E go dey okay if I sit here small?

1755.translation: My hand dey pain me, so I no fit write.

1756.translation: For plain present verb, add ㄴ다 after vowel or 는다 after consonant. Describing words and 있다/없다 just add 다.

1757.translation: My younger sibling dey read book.

1760.translation: Plain past na -았/었다; plain future na -(으)ㄹ 것이다; nouns take -(이)다.

1768.translation: My elder brother dey rest for house.

1770.translation: Verbs wey end with ㄹ drop am before ㄴ and add ㄴ다.

1775.translation: Casual plain questions end with -니 or -냐. Dem dey attach to stem; for past, use -았/었니.

1781.translation: person go do something, plain form

1782.translation: Today na Sunday. I meet friend. We watch film together.

1784.translation: Sun dey set early for winter.

1785.translation: This river start for mountains and flow enter sea.

1786.translation: The novel wey I read yesterday interesting pass wetin I expect well-well.

1788.translation: These days, I dey trek one hour every morning. E hard at first, but e don become habit now. After the walk, my head dey clear and I fit start the day with energy. I plan to continue this habit.

1789.translation: I no fit chop because I dey study.

1790.translation: -느라고 dey attach to verb stem and give reason for result wey usually negative. The two clauses get the same subject.

1791.translation: I no fit sleep because I dey do homework.

1792.translation: I miss call because I dey talk with friend.

1795.translation: I no do homework because I dey play games.

1796.translation: I no hear bell because I dey listen to music.

1797.translation: I wake up late because I dey read till late.

1798.translation: I no fit watch film because I dey take photos.

1799.translation: I no fit do homework because I dey look after my younger sibling.

1800.translation: I busy these days because I dey prepare for exam.

1801.translation: Even though snow dey fall, people plenty.

1802.translation: -는데도 / -(으)ㄴ데도 mean even though. Use -는데도 after verbs and 있다/없다; use -(으)ㄴ데도 after describing words.

1803.translation: Even though I study well-well, I no do well for exam.

1804.translation: Past tense dey come before -는데도 as -았/었는데도, but no put past ending before -느라고.

1805.translation: Even though I chop plenty, hunger dey catch me.

1806.translation: Even though weather cold, I dey exercise outside.

1807.translation: Even though I take medicine, my head dey pain me.

1808.translation: Even though I no get money, I buy expensive clothes.

1809.translation: Even though I dey practise often, Korean hard.

1810.translation: Even though teacher explain, I still no understand well.

1811.translation: Even though price high, people plenty.

1812.translation: Even though I no well, I go school.

1813.translation: Even though I get plenty time, I no do homework.

1814.translation: Even though na night, outside bright.

1815.translation: Even though I wake up early, I late.

1816.translation: Even though the person short, the person sabi play basketball.

1817.translation: I no fit often go club meetings because I dey do part-time work.

1818.translation: Even though road hold up, bus always dey reach on time.

1819.translation: I even forget to chop afternoon food because I dey write report.

1820.translation: Even though I wear thick coat, wind cold and I continue to shiver.

1821.translation: Even though our house small, friends dey often come visit.

1822.translation: Because I dey help workmate, I no fit finish my own work before closing time.

1823.translation: My friend ask whether I get time tomorrow.

1824.translation: For reported questions, use -냐고 with verbs, describing words and 있다/없다; past na -았/었냐고. Nouns take (이)냐고. 묻다 or 하다 follow am.

1825.translation: Teacher ask where I dey go.

1826.translation: My younger sibling ask wetin we dey chop for evening.

1827.translation: My mama ask whether I don chop.

1828.translation: My friend ask whether this bag expensive.

1829.translation: The pikin ask wetin this be.

1830.translation: Person ask whether that person na student.

1831.translation: My friend ask wetin I do for weekend.

1832.translation: My elder sister ask whether rain go fall tomorrow.

1833.translation: For future reported question, use -(으)ㄹ 거냐고. Verbs wey end with ㄹ drop ㄹ before 냐고.

1835.translation: Friend ask where I dey live.

1836.translation: My papa ask wetin time I dey come.

1837.translation: Friend ask whether I don watch the film.

1838.translation: Shop attendant ask how many people dey.

1839.translation: My younger sibling ask when I go Korea.

1840.translation: Friend ask where I dey now.

1841.translation: My mama ask whether I no get homework.

1843.translation: Friend ask whether I like Korean food.

1844.translation: Person wey I no know ask wetin time e be now.

1845.translation: My younger sibling dey ask whether I don read this book.

1846.translation: Friend ask whether I go follow go.

1849.translation: My mama dey ask whether I don finish all homework.

1851.translation: You no catch wetin the other person just talk, so you ask make the person repeat am.

1852.translation: Teacher say make we keep quiet.

1853.translation: Reported command na -(으)라고 하다: use -으라고 after consonant, and -라고 after vowel or ㄹ. Reported suggestion na -자고 하다.

1854.translation: My mama say make I sleep early.

1855.translation: Friend suggest make we watch film together.

1856.translation: Doctor say make I take the medicine.

1857.translation: My papa say make I close door.

1858.translation: Friend suggest make we relax together for weekend.

1859.translation: My younger sibling suggest make we chop afternoon food together.

1860.translation: Friend suggest make we meet early tomorrow.

1861.translation: My mama say make I do homework first.

1862.translation: Friend talk say make person call me.

1863.translation: My elder sister say make I wait here.

1864.translation: Teacher say make we speak Korean.

1865.translation: Friend say make person come our house.

1866.translation: Doctor say make I no drink alcohol.

1867.translation: For reported negative command, use -지 말라고. For negative suggestion, use -지 말자고.

1868.translation: Friend suggest make we no go there.

1869.translation: Teacher say make I open window.

1870.translation: Verbs wey end with ㄹ take -라고, no be -으라고, for reported commands.

1871.translation: Friend suggest make we take photo together.

1872.translation: My mama say make I carry umbrella.

1873.translation: Friend suggest make we study together because exam dey tomorrow.

1874.translation: My papa say make I get up quick.

1875.translation: Teacher say make we look blackboard.

1876.translation: Friend suggest make we go drink coffee.

1877.translation: Teacher say make we open our books.

1878.translation: Minsu say Minsu dey come tomorrow.

1879.translation: To report statement, verbs take -ㄴ/는다고 하다, describing words and 있다/없다 take plain -다고, and nouns take (이)라고.

1881.translation: My younger sibling say hunger dey catch am.

1883.translation: My mama say rain go fall this evening.

1884.translation: For past or future event, use -았/었다고 or -(으)ㄹ 거라고 before 하다.

1885.translation: My papa say e dey drive now.

1886.translation: Dem say that person na doctor.

1887.translation: That person say na my friend elder brother.

1888.translation: My friend talk say my friend no well yesterday.

1889.translation: My younger sibling say my younger sibling watch film yesterday.

1890.translation: My friend say e dey chop now.

1891.translation: My elder sister say e dey exercise every day.

1892.translation: News talk say snow go fall tomorrow.

1893.translation: My friend talk say Korean food sweet.

1894.translation: My younger sibling say e no get homework.

1895.translation: My boyfriend say e busy these days.

1896.translation: My friend say e no dey go school today.

1897.translation: My younger sibling say e dey relax for house.

1898.translation: Verbs wey end with ㄹ drop ㄹ before ㄴ when dem dey form plain present.

1899.translation: My friend say e dey live for Seoul.

1902.translation: I talk say I dey okay.

1903.translation: The student say e want study Korean.

1904.translation: The pikin talk say e no want go school.

1905.translation: A: Why Minsu no come? B: Minsu talk say Minsu catch cold, so Minsu no fit come today.

1906.translation: My younger sibling dey pretend say e no well.

1907.translation: For present verbs and 있다/없다, -는 척하다 mean pretend to do something. After describing words and 이다, use -(으)ㄴ 척하다.

1908.translation: My friend pretend say e don finish all homework.

1909.translation: To pretend say person don already do something, use past -(으)ㄴ 척하다 on verb.

1910.translation: That person dey pretend say e rich.

1911.translation: I pretend say I no see teacher.

1912.translation: I pretend say I dey okay, but actually I sad.

1913.translation: My friend dey pretend say e sabi Korean well.

1914.translation: My younger sibling dey pretend to study, but dey play games.

1915.translation: That student pretend say e understand teacher words.

1916.translation: The pikin pretend say e no dey cry.

1917.translation: Negative fit enter inside the pretense. 안 + verb or -지 않다 become 안 V는 척 or V지 않는 척.

1918.translation: My friend pretend say e no hear phone call.

1919.translation: My younger sibling pretend say e no vex.

1920.translation: That person dey pretend say e kind, but actually e no be so.

1921.translation: My younger sibling dey act like adult.

1922.translation: The pikin pretend say e no sick.

1923.translation: My elder brother dey act like nothing happen.

1924.translation: I pretend say I don take medicine.

1925.translation: My friend pretend say e don pay.

1926.translation: I pretend to smile, but I no feel good inside.

1927.translation: My younger sibling just dey pretend to clean, then dey play.

1928.translation: My friend pretend say e don go Korea before.

1929.translation: My younger sibling pretend say e wake up early.

1930.translation: The more I study Korean, the more e dey interesting.

1931.translation: -(으)ㄹ수록 mean the more one thing happen, the more another thing happen. E dey attach to verb and describing-word stems. Stems wey end with ㄹ take -수록 directly.

1932.translation: The more I chop these snacks, the more I want chop.

1933.translation: As person dey older, time dey move faster.

1934.translation: The more you talk with friend, the closer una dey become.

1935.translation: The higher you go, the colder e dey.

1936.translation: The cheaper the price, the better.

1937.translation: The farther the distance, the higher the taxi fare.

1938.translation: The harder e be, the harder you need work.

1939.translation: For ㅂ- and ㄷ-irregular stems, the last sound dey change before -(으)ㄹ수록.

1940.translation: The colder weather be, the sweeter warm tea dey.

1941.translation: Na song wey dey sound better the more you listen.

1942.translation: The more I use am, the more comfortable e dey.

1943.translation: The more I practise, the better I dey do.

1944.translation: The earlier you go, the better.

1945.translation: The bigger e be, the more e dey cost.

1946.translation: If you work hard, e natural say good result go follow.

1947.translation: -기 마련이다 dey show say something normally go happen or na natural result. E dey attach to plain stem.

1948.translation: After winter pass, spring normally go follow.

1949.translation: Na normal thing say everybody go find am hard at first.

1950.translation: Things normally dey spoil when person use dem for long time.

1952.translation: When rain fall, road normally dey hold up.

1953.translation: If you sleep late, you normally go tire.

1955.translation: When you spend money, e naturally dey finish.

1957.translation: Verb stem + -(으)ㄹ 걸 그랬어요 dey show regret about something wey you no do, like I for don do am.

1959.translation: I for try wear that cloth.

1967.translation: I for chop morning food before I come.

1972.translation: Use -지 말 걸 그랬어요 to show regret about something wey you do, like I for no do am.

1973.translation: I for no play till late yesterday.

1981.translation: I for give my friend present.

1982.translation: I for charge my phone ahead.

1983.translation: -(으)ㄹ 걸 그랬어요 show regret about something wey you no do. For something wey you do and now regret, use -지 말 걸 그랬어요. Verb before 걸 always take -(으)ㄹ form.

1984.translation: If I know say road go hold up, I for enter subway.

1985.translation: I for revise one more time before exam.

1986.translation: I for no vex like that.

1987.translation: I for listen to my friend finish.

1988.translation: A: You do well for exam? B: No. I for study more. A: No worry too much. Make we prepare together next time. B: Thank you. Make we study together for library.

1990.translation: Match the reporting ending with the kind of speech: statement -다고, question -냐고, command -(으)라고, suggestion -자고.

1993.translation: My younger sibling suggest make we play game together.

1994.translation: I miss call because I dey clean.

1995.translation: This revision dey mix reported speech, complex connectors and earlier bridge grammar for the level.

1996.translation: Even though my belle full, I chop cake.

1997.translation: The more I chop Korean food, the sweeter e dey.
